topics.title: Basic Reflexive & Pronominal Verbs
topics.objective: Form and conjugate basic reflexive and pronominal verbs (*se laver, s'appeler, se lever, se coucher*) using reflexive pronouns (*me, te, se, nous, vous, se*).

topics.title: Basic Sentence Structure & Adverb Placement
topics.objective: Construct standard declarative sentences following Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) order and place basic frequency/manner adverbs (*toujours, souvent, bien, mal*) correctly.

topics.title: Basic Negation (Ne ... pas / N' ... pas) & Article Mutation

topics.title: Interrogative Sentences & Question Words
topics.objective: Form questions using intonation, *Est-ce que*, pronoun inversion, and interrogative words (*qui, que, où, quand, pourquoi, comment, combien*).

topics.title: Telling Time in French
topics.objective: Ask for and express time using *Il est... heure(s)*, fixed expressions for quarters (*et quart*, *moins le quart*), half-hours (*et demie* / *et demi*), noon/midnight (*midi*, *minuit*), exact hours (*pile*), and time of day indicators (*du matin*, *de l'après-midi*, *du soir*).

topics.title: Basic Prepositions of Place (Location & Spatial Position)
topics.objective: Express physical position, spatial relationships, and location using simple prepositions (*dans, sur, sous, devant, derrière, entre*) and compound prepositional locutions (*à côté de, en face de, près de*), including mandatory article contraction rules (*de + le = du*, *de + les = des*).

topics.spacy_pattern:
# Pattern 1: Stressed Pronoun after Preposition (e.g., avec moi, pour eux, chez elle)
pattern_prep_stressed = [
    {"POS": "ADP"},
    {
        "POS": "PRON",
        "LEMMA": {
            "IN": [
                "moi",
                "toi",
                "lui",
                "elle",
                "nous",
                "vous",
                "eux",
                "elles",
                "soi",
            ]
        },
        "MORPH": {"REGEX": "PronType=(Prs|Emp)"},
    },
]

# Pattern 2: Stressed Pronoun for Subject Emphasis / Dislocation (e.g., Moi, je...)
pattern_emphasis_stressed = [
    {
        "POS": "PRON",
        "LEMMA": {
            "IN": [
                "moi",
                "toi",
                "lui",
                "elle",
                "nous",
                "vous",
                "eux",
                "elles",
                "soi",
            ]
        },
        "MORPH": {"REGEX": "PronType=(Prs|Emp)"},
    },
    {"TEXT": ","},
    {"POS": "PRON", "MORPH": {"REGEX": "PronType=Prs"}},
]

# Pattern 3: Stressed Pronoun after C'est / Ce sont
pattern_cest_stressed = [
    {"LEMMA": "ce", "POS": "PRON"},
    {"LEMMA": "être", "POS": "AUX"},
    {
        "POS": "PRON",
        "LEMMA": {
            "IN": [
                "moi",
                "toi",
                "lui",
                "elle",
                "nous",
                "vous",
                "eux",
                "elles",
                "soi",
            ]
        },
        "MORPH": {"REGEX": "PronType=(Prs|Emp)"},
    },
]

# Pattern 4: Stressed Pronoun in Comparison (e.g., plus grand que moi)

    {"POS": "ADV", "LEMMA": {"IN": ["plus", "moins", "aussi"]}},
    {"POS": "ADJ"},
    {"POS": "SCONJ", "LEMMA": "que"},
    {
        "POS": "PRON",
        "LEMMA": {
            "IN": [
                "moi",
                "toi",
                "lui",
                "elle",
                "nous",

topics.title: Existential Expression & Temporal Ago: Il y a
topics.objective: Master the existential expression *il y a* (there is / there are), its negative form *il n'y a pas de*, and its temporal usage *il y a + [time]* (ago).
topics.spacy_pattern:
# Pattern 1: Existential Affirmative "Il y a + DET"
pattern_il_y_a_aff = [
    {"POS": "PRON", "LEMMA": "il", "DEP": {"IN": ["nsubj:expl", "nsubj"]}},
    {"POS": "PRON", "LEMMA": "y", "DEP": "expl"},
    {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "avoir"},
    {"POS": {"IN": ["DET", "NUM", "ADV"]}, "OP": "?"},
]

# Pattern 2: Existential Negative "Il n'y a pas de / d'"
pattern_il_y_a_neg = [
    {"POS": "PRON", "LEMMA": "il", "DEP": {"IN": ["nsubj:expl", "nsubj"]}},
    {"POS": "ADV", "LEMMA": "ne"},
    {"POS": "PRON", "LEMMA": "y", "DEP": "expl"},
    {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "avoir"},
    {"POS": "ADV", "LEMMA": "pas"},
    {"POS": {"IN": ["ADP", "DET"]}, "LEMMA": "de"},
]

# Pattern 3: Temporal Ago "il y a + NUM + NOUN (time unit)"
pattern_il_y_a_temp = [
    {"POS": "PRON", "LEMMA": "il"},
    {"POS": "PRON", "LEMMA": "y"},
    {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "avoir"},
    {"POS": "NUM"},
    {"POS": "NOUN", "LEMMA": {"IN": ["minute", "heure", "jour", "semaine", "mois", "an", "année"]}},
]

topics.title: Demonstrative Adjectives (Ce, Cet, Cette, Ces, -ci, -là)
topics.objective: Select and apply the appropriate demonstrative adjective (*ce, cet, cette, ces*) based on noun gender, number, and phonetics (vowel/silent h), and use suffix particles (*-ci*, *-là*) for spatial/temporal distinction and contrast.

topics.title: Days of the Week, Months, Seasons, and Date Expressions

topics.title: Aspectual Uses of the Imparfait: Habitual Actions, Descriptions, & Background States
topics.objective: Apply l'imparfait appropriately to convey uncompleted past actions, habitual/iterative past routines, physical and emotional descriptions, weather conditions, time, and background contexts.

topics.title: Passé Composé vs Imparfait Contrast & Interrupted Actions
topics.objective: Contrast completed specific events (Passé Composé) with background continuous states or ongoing actions (Imparfait) within single and compound complex sentences.

topics.title: Past Temporal Expressions & Duration Markers (Depuis, Pendant, Il y a, En)
topics.objective: Distinguish and correctly deploy past time prepositions (*depuis*, *pendant*, *il y a*, *en*, *dans*) to anchor past actions, duration, and elapsed time relative to the moment of speech.

topics.title: Formation & Syntax of the Futur Simple
topics.objective: Form and apply the simple future tense across regular and irregular verbs for predictions, formal commitments, plans, and conditional main clauses.

topics.title: Conditionnel Présent: Polite Requests, Desires, & Potentialities
topics.objective: Construct and utilize the present conditional by combining future stems with imperfect endings to communicate politeness, wishes, advice, and unconfirmed information.

topics.title: Hypothetical Constructions with Si Clauses (Real & Unreal Conditionals)
topics.objective: Formulate Type 1 (open/real conditions) and Type 2 (unreal/present hypothetical conditions) complex sentences governed by the conjunction *si*.

topics.title: Futur Antérieur & Temporal Conjunctions (Quand, Lorsque, Dès que)
topics.objective: Construct the compound future anterior tense (auxiliary in Futur Simple + Past Participle) to express actions that will be completed prior to another future action.

topics.title: Direct (COD) and Indirect (COI) Object Pronouns
topics.objective: Identify, substitute, and correctly position direct object pronouns (*me, te, le, la, nous, vous, les*) and indirect object pronouns (*lui, leur*) in simple and compound tenses.

topics.title: Adverbial Pronouns Y (Location/À + Noun) and EN (Quantity/De + Noun)
topics.objective: Substitute prepositional phrases of location/destination (*à, en, dans, sur* + place) with *y*, and expressions of quantity/indefinite items (*de, du, de la, des* + noun) with *en*.

topics.title: Double Object Pronoun Order & Sentence Syntax
topics.objective: Apply the multi-pronoun ordering chart across declarative, negative, and imperative clause structures containing multiple object pronouns.

topics.title: Relative Pronouns (Qui, Que, Où, Dont)
topics.objective: Link independent clauses and replace repetitive antecedents using simple relative pronouns based on syntactic function (*qui* = subject, *que* = direct object, *où* = place/time, *dont* = complement with *de*).

topics.title: Stressed Pronouns (Pronoms Toniques: Moi, Toi, Lui, Elle, Soi, Nous, Vous, Eux, Elles)
topics.objective: Employ disjunctive/stressed pronouns for emphasis, after prepositions, after *c'est/ce sont*, in compound subjects, and in short answers.

topics.title: Possessive Pronouns (Le mien, La tienne, Les leurs, etc.)
topics.objective: Form and correctly agree possessive pronouns in gender and number with the replaced noun, preceded by the appropriate definite article.

topics.title: Demonstrative Pronouns (Celui, Celle, Ceux, Celles, Celui-ci, Celui-là)
topics.objective: Construct simple and compound demonstrative pronouns to replace previously mentioned nouns, specified by relative clauses, prepositions (*de*), or proximity suffixes (*-ci / -là*).

topics.title: Prepositions with Geographical Names (En, À, Au, Aux, De, Du, Des)
topics.objective: Select correct prepositions of place and origin (*en, à, au, aux, de, du, des*) based on the grammatical gender, number, and initial letter of countries, continents, islands, and cities.

topics.title: Causative Construction (Faire + Infinitif & Se Faire + Infinitif)
topics.objective: Master the causative structure (*faire* + infinitive, *se faire* + infinitive) to express causing an action to be performed by someone else, managing word order, pronoun placement before *faire*, and introducing agents with *par* or *à*.

topics.title: Concordance and Sequence of Tenses in Subordinate Clauses (La Concordance des Temps)
topics.objective: Apply the correct tense shifts (sequence of tenses / concordance des temps) in subordinate clauses based on the tense of the main reporting clause across direct/indirect speech and complex sentence structures.

topics.title: Infinitive Negation & Word Order (Ne pas, Ne jamais, Ne plus + Infinitif)
topics.objective: Form negated infinitive clauses correctly by placing negative adverbial pairs (*ne pas*, *ne jamais*, *ne plus*, *ne rien*) immediately before the infinitive verb, while positioning object and reflexive pronouns between the negative pair and the infinitive.

topics.title: Introduction to the Subjunctive Mood (Le Subjonctif Présent)
topics.objective: Understand the fundamental mood distinction between indicative objective reality and subjunctive subjective reality, master the 5 core trigger categories, and apply regular stem formation rules (-e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent) as the gateway to B2 advanced subjunctive structures.

topics.title: Impersonal Expressions: General Infinitive (de + inf) vs Specific Subjunctive (que + subjonctif)
topics.objective: Distinguish and master impersonal expressions (*il est possible*, *il vaut mieux*, *il est important*, *il s'agit de*, *il convient de*) contrasting general statements using *de* + infinitive against specific-subject subclauses using *que* + subjunctive.

exercises.fr: Il est important que vous étudiez.

topics.objective: Form the French gerund (`en` + present participle stem `-ant`), master its adverbial functions (simultaneity, manner/means, condition, cause), enforce the strict subject co-referentiality constraint, and distinguish the invariant verbal gerund/participle from the variable verbal adjective (*adjectif verbal*).

topics.title: Present Subjunctive Regular Stems & Conjugation (Subjonctif Présent - Régulier)
topics.objective: Form and apply the present subjunctive of regular -er, -ir, and -re verbs in dependent clauses after triggers expressing necessity, desire, and uncertainty.

topics.title: Irregular Subjunctive Verbs (Subjonctif des Verbes Irréguliers)
topics.objective: Correctly conjugate and employ high-frequency irregular verbs in the present subjunctive (*être, avoir, faire, aller, pouvoir, savoir, vouloir*).

topics.title: Subjunctive Semantic Triggers & Modal Matrix Clauses
topics.objective: Identify and systematically apply subjunctive mood across five primary semantic categories: Volition, Emotion, Impersonal Necessity, Doubt, and Complex Conjunctions.

topics.title: Subjunctive vs. Indicative Contrastive Syntax (Subjonctif ou Indicatif)
topics.objective: Contrast indicative and subjunctive usage based on clause polarity, assertion level, and matrix predicate certainty (*penser, croire, espérer, être certain*).

topics.title: Past Subjunctive (Subjonctif Passé)
topics.objective: Form and deploy the past subjunctive using present subjunctive auxiliaries (*avoir* / *être*) + past participle to express completed past actions in dependent clauses.

topics.title: Pluperfect Tense (Plus-que-parfait) Formation & Antecedency
topics.objective: Construct and use the pluperfect tense (*imparfait* of auxiliary + past participle) to establish temporal antecedency between two past events.

topics.title: Pluperfect Agreement Rules & Type 3 Conditionals (Si + Plus-que-parfait)
topics.objective: Apply past participle agreement rules in pluperfect constructions and formulate counterfactual hypothetical sentences (Conditionnel Type 3).

topics.title: Future Perfect (Futur Antérieur) Formation & Chronological Aspect
topics.objective: Form and apply the future perfect tense (*futur simple* of auxiliary + past participle) to denote actions that will be completed prior to a specified future moment or event.

topics.title: Future Perfect with Temporal Conjunctions (Quand, Dès que, Lorsque)
topics.objective: Apply the obligatory double-future rule in French temporal subordinate clauses using *quand, lorsque, dès que, aussitôt que, une fois que*.

modules.name: Passive Voice, Indirect Speech & Complex Prepositional Verbs

topics.title: Passive Voice (Voix Passive) Formation & Agent Prepositions
topics.objective: Transform active sentences into the passive voice across multiple tenses, selecting correct agent prepositions (*par* vs *de*).

topics.title: Passive Tense Variations & Pronominal Passive Alternatives
topics.objective: Master passive voice across compound/modal tenses and utilize natural pronominal passive alternatives (*se faire*, *se voir*, *se + verb*).

topics.title: Indirect Speech (Discours Indirect) Tense Shifts in Past Contexts
topics.objective: Convert direct statements into indirect speech after past matrix reporting verbs, applying obligatory backshifting tense rules.

topics.title: Indirect Questions & Imperatives in Indirect Speech
topics.objective: Transform direct interrogatives and imperatives into indirect reporting clauses using *si, ce que, ce qui*, interrogative adverbs, and *de + infinitive*.

topics.title: Complex Prepositional Verbs Followed by De (Verbes + De + Infinitif/Nom)
topics.objective: Master B2-level verbal governing structures requiring preposition *de* before infinitive complements or nominal objects.

topics.title: Complex Prepositional Verbs Followed by À (Verbes + À + Infinitif/Nom)
topics.objective: Master B2-level verbal governing structures requiring preposition *à* before infinitive complements or indirect objects.

topics.title: Expressions of Cause & Consequence (Expression de Cause et Conséquence)
topics.objective: Formulate complex argumentative sentences expressing logical causality and consequence using advanced connectors (*puisque, grâce à, à cause de, c'est pourquoi, par conséquent*).

topics.title: All 3 Si-Clause Types: Real, Unreal Present & Counterfactual Past (Système Hypothétique Complet)
topics.objective: Synthesize, differentiate, and master all three standard conditional sentence structures with *si* (real/probable present-future, unreal present hypothesis, counterfactual past hypothesis) in single or multi-clause discourse contexts.
topics.spacy_pattern:
# Matcher patterns targeting all 3 Si-clause types in French

# Type 1: Si + Présent -> Futur Simple / Présent / Impératif
pattern_type1 = [
    {"LEMMA": "si", "POS": "SCONJ"},
    {"OP": "*"},
    {"POS": "VERB", "MORPH": {"IN": ["Mood=Ind|Tense=Pres", "Tense=Pres"]}},
    {"OP": "*"},
    {"POS": "VERB", "MORPH": {"IN": ["Mood=Ind|Tense=Fut", "Tense=Fut", "Mood=Imp", "Mood=Ind|Tense=Pres"]}}
]

# Type 2: Si + Imparfait -> Conditionnel Présent
pattern_type2 = [
    {"LEMMA": "si", "POS": "SCONJ"},
    {"OP": "*"},
    {"POS": "VERB", "MORPH": {"IN": ["Mood=Ind|Tense=Imp", "Tense=Imp"]}},
    {"OP": "*"},
    {"POS": "VERB", "MORPH": {"IN": ["Mood=Cnd|Tense=Pres", "Mood=Cnd"]}}
]

# Type 3: Si + Plus-que-parfait -> Conditionnel Passé
pattern_type3 = [
    {"LEMMA": "si", "POS": "SCONJ"},
    {"OP": "*"},
    {"LEMMA": {"IN": ["avoir", "être"]}, "MORPH": {"IN": ["Mood=Ind|Tense=Imp", "Tense=Imp"]}},
    {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
    {"POS": "VERB", "MORPH": {"IN": ["VerbForm=Part|Tense=Past", "Aspect=Perf"]}},
    {"OP": "*"},
    {"LEMMA": {"IN": ["avoir", "être"]}, "MORPH": {"IN": ["Mood=Cnd|Tense=Pres", "Mood=Cnd"]}},
    {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
    {"POS": "VERB", "MORPH": {"IN": ["VerbForm=Part|Tense=Past", "Aspect=Perf"]}}
]

topics.title: Advanced Logical Connectors & Discourse Markers (Connecteurs Logiques et Marqueurs du Discours)
topics.objective: Master and correctly deploy advanced discourse connectors and logical markers expressing Concession, Opposition, Consequence, and Addition in formal written and spoken French.

topics.title: Compound Relative Pronouns (Lequel / Laquelle / Lesquels / Lesquelles & Contracted Forms)
topics.objective: Form and correctly position compound relative pronouns (*lequel, laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles*) and their contractions (*auquel, auxquels, auquel, auxquelles, duquel, desquels, duquel, desquelles*) after prepositions to introduce non-human or precise antecedent relative clauses.

topics.title: Conditional Perfect / Past Conditional (Conditionnel Passé)
topics.objective: Construct and deploy the past conditional to express past hypotheticals, regret, reproach, and unconfirmed past news or statements.

topics.title: Nominalisation of Verbal Actions & Adjectives (La Nominalisation)
topics.objective: Convert active verbal clauses and adjectival predicates into formal, compact noun phrases using derivational suffixation (-tion, -ment, -age, -ure, -ité, -ence/ance) and genitive *de* complements in journalistic and formal registers.

topics.title: Emphatic Cleft Constructions (Phrases Clivées : c'est... qui / que, ce qui... c'est, ce que... c'est)
topics.objective: Form, analyze, and apply emphatic cleft sentences (*c'est... qui*, *c'est... que*, *ce qui... c'est*, *ce que... c'est*, *ce dont... c'est*) to highlight sentence elements (subject, direct object, prepositional/adverbial complement) and establish contrastive focus in written and spoken discourse.
topics.spacy_pattern:
# Pattern 1: Standard Cleft (c'est / ce sont + [Focus Element] + qui / que / qu')
pattern_cleft_standard = [
    {"LOWER": {"IN": ["c'", "ce"]}},
    {"LEMMA": "être", "POS": {"IN": ["AUX", "VERB"]}},
    {"OP": "+"},  # Intermediate focused element (noun phrase, pronoun, prepositional phrase, adverb)
    {"LOWER": {"IN": ["qui", "que", "qu'"]}, "POS": {"IN": ["PRON", "SCONJ"]}}
]

# Pattern 2: Pseudo-cleft / Reversed Cleft (ce qui / ce que / ce dont ... c'est / ce sont)
pattern_pseudo_cleft = [
    {"LOWER": "ce"},
    {"LOWER": {"IN": ["qui", "que", "qu'", "dont"]}},
    {"OP": "+"},
    {"LOWER": {"IN": ["c'", "ce"]}},
    {"LEMMA": "être", "POS": {"IN": ["AUX", "VERB"]}}
]

topics.title: The Imperfect Subjunctive (Le Subjonctif Imparfait)
topics.objective: Understand and recognize the literary imperfect subjunctive used in classical literature, formal discourse, and elevated writing after past main verbs.

topics.title: The Pluperfect Subjunctive (Le Plus-que-parfait du Subjonctif)
topics.objective: Master the compound literary subjunctive tense to express completed past actions that occurred prior to another past event under subjunctive-triggering conditions.

topics.title: Advanced Subjunctive Triggers & Complex Conjunctions
topics.objective: Identify and correctly deploy rare, formal, and elevated conjunctions that require the subjunctive mood in academic and literary contexts.

topics.title: Subjunctive with Ne Explétif (Le Ne Explétif)
topics.objective: Apply and recognize the non-negative formal *ne explétif* in formal writing after verbs and conjunctions of fear, avoidance, prevention, and condition.

topics.title: The Simple Past Tense (Le Passé Simple)
topics.objective: Master the formation, recognition, and literary deployment of the *passé simple* tense in historical narratives, literature, and formal texts.

topics.title: The Past Anterior Tense (Le Passé Antérieur)
topics.objective: Form and correctly utilize the *passé antérieur* to express a completed action that occurred immediately prior to another action expressed in the *passé simple*.

topics.title: Advanced Historical & Narrative Syntax (Passé Simple vs Imparfait vs Passé Antérieur)
topics.objective: Master the complex interaction of literary past tenses (*passé simple*, *imparfait*, *passé antérieur*, *plus-que-parfait*) to structure multi-layered historical narratives.

modules.name: Advanced Syntax, Discourse Markers & N'importe/Quelque Expressions

topics.title: Indefinite Expressions with N'importe (N'importe quel / qui / quoi / où / quand / comment)
topics.objective: Accurately form and deploy all indefinite expressions with *n'importe* to express complete indifference or universal selection ("any", "whoever", "whatever", "anywhere").

topics.title: Advanced Indefinite Structures with Quelque (Quelque... que + Subjunctive, Quelconque, Quelque part)
topics.objective: Master advanced indefinite constructions with *quelque*, including concession clauses (*quelque + adj + que + subj*) and indefinite pronouns.

topics.title: Participial Clauses, Present Participles & Gerunds (Participe Présent, Gérondif & Participe Passé Absolu)
topics.objective: Form and utilize non-finite participial clauses (*participe présent*, *gérondif*, *participe absolu*) to condense subordinate clauses in formal academic French.

topics.title: Nuanced Modals & Inverted Conditionals (Would, Could, Should & Inverted Hypotheticals)
topics.objective: Express subtle shades of obligation, possibility, regret, and hypothetical inversion using advanced modal verbs (*devoir*, *pouvoir*, *vouloir*) and literary inverted conditionals.

topics.title: Sophisticated Discourse Markers & Logical Connectors
topics.objective: Use complex discourse connectors (*alors que*, *tandis que*, *ne... que*, *tant que*, *d'autant plus que*, *or*, *en revanche*) to structure formal argumentation.

topics.title: Literary & Formal Subject-Verb Inversion (Inversion Stylistique & Sujet Inversé)
topics.objective: Master literary and formal subject-verb inversion patterns in French, including inversion after initial adverbs, incise/reporting clauses after direct speech, and complex inversion with subject pronoun duplication.
topics.spacy_pattern:
# spaCy Matcher patterns for Stylistic & Formal Inversion
pattern_inversion = [
    # Pattern 1: Initial Adverb + Conjugated Verb + Hyphenated Pronoun Subject
    [
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["peut-être", "ainsi", "toujours", "encore"]}},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}},
        {"LOWER": "-t-", "OP": "?"},
        {"POS": "PRON", "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["PronType=Prs"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 2: Multi-word initial adverbs (à peine, sans doute, en vain, du moins) + Verb + Pronoun
    [
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["à", "sans", "en", "du"]}},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["peine", "doute", "vain", "moins"]}},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}},
        {"LOWER": "-t-", "OP": "?"},
        {"POS": "PRON", "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["PronType=Prs"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 3: Complex Inversion with Noun Duplication (Noun + Verb + Pronoun)
    [
        {"POS": "NOUN"},
        {"OP": "*"},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}},
        {"LOWER": "-t-", "OP": "?"},
        {"POS": "PRON", "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["PronType=Prs"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 4: Incise Reporting Inversion after quoted speech
    [
        {"ORTH": {"IN": ["»", "\"", "''"]}},
        {"POS": "PUNCT", "OP": "?"},
        {"POS": "VERB", "LEMMA": {"IN": ["dire", "répondre", "ajouter", "s'exclamer", "poursuivre", "demander", "chuchoter", "affirmer"]}},
        {"LOWER": "-t-", "OP": "?"},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["PRON", "NOUN", "PROPN"]}}
    ]
]

topics.title: Compound & Literary Negation (Ne...guère, Ne...nul, Ne...nullement, Ne...point & Ne Explétif)
topics.objective: Synthesize grammatical rules and master formal deployment of compound/literary negative adverbs (*ne...guère*, *ne...nul/nulle*, *ne...nullement*, *ne...point*) and the non-negative *ne explétif* in subordinate clauses following verbs/conjunctions of fear, doubt, prevention, and temporal precedence.
topics.spacy_pattern:
# spaCy Matcher patterns for Literary Negation & Ne Explétif
pattern_complex_negation = [
    # Pattern 1: Literary Negative Adverbs (ne...guère / point / nullement / aucunement)
    [
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["ne", "n'"]}},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "OP": "?"},
        {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["guère", "point", "nullement", "aucunement"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 2: Negative Determiner / Pronoun (nul / nulle)
    [
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["nul", "nulle"]}},
        {"OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["ne", "n'"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 3: Ne Explétif after fear/prevention/doubt verbs or conjunctions
    [
        {"LEMMA": {"IN": ["craindre", "redouter", "empêcher", "douter", "nier", "avant", "peur", "crainte", "moins"]}},
        {"OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": "que"},
        {"OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["ne", "n'"]}, "POS": "ADV"},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["Mood=Sub"]}}
    ]
]

topics.title: Pro-form Substitution & Ellipsis in Discourse (Neuter Pronouns & VP Ellipsis)
topics.objective: Master clause-level pro-form substitution using neuter pronouns (*le*, *en*, *y*) to replace entire propositions or clausal complements, and apply VP ellipsis patterns in formal conversational dynamics.

topics.title: Restrictive & Exclusive Constructions (Le Ne...que, Seulement, Uniquement, Rien que & Exclusions)
topics.objective: Master the nuances, stylistic variations, and syntactic constraints of restrictive (*ne...que*, *ne faire que + infinitif*) and exclusive modifiers (*seulement*, *uniquement*, *rien que*, *à l'exception de*, *hormis*, *excepté*) across register levels.

topics.title: Advanced Concession Conjunctions (si tant est que, pour autant que, à supposer que, en admettant que, quelque... que)
topics.objective: Master high-register concessive conjunctions requiring the subjunctive mood (*si tant est que*, *pour autant que*, *à supposer que*, *en admettant que*, *quelque... que*) and contrast them with indicative concessives (*bien que* / *quoique* + subjunctive vs. *si tant est que* + high-hypothetical subjunctive vs. indicative concessive markers).
topics.spacy_pattern:
# spaCy Matcher patterns for Advanced Concession Conjunctions requiring Subjunctive
pattern = [
    # Pattern 1: si tant est que + Subjunctive
    [
        {"LOWER": "si"},
        {"LOWER": "tant"},
        {"LOWER": "est"},
        {"LOWER": "que"},
        {"OP": "*"},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["Mood=Sub"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 2: pour autant que + Subjunctive
    [
        {"LOWER": "pour"},
        {"LOWER": "autant"},
        {"LOWER": "que"},
        {"OP": "*"},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["Mood=Sub"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 3: à supposer que / en admettant que + Subjunctive
    [
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["à", "a", "en"]}},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["supposer", "admettant"]}},
        {"LOWER": "que"},
        {"OP": "*"},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["Mood=Sub"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 4: quelque + ADJ + que + Subjunctive
    [
        {"LEMMA": "quelque"},
        {"POS": "ADJ"},
        {"LOWER": "que"},
        {"OP": "*"},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["Mood=Sub"]}}
    ]
]

topics.title: Mixed Conditionals (Les Conditionnels Mixtes: Si + Plus-que-parfait / Imparfait)
topics.objective: Synthesize and master mixed conditional structures combining different tense frames across hypothetical clauses to express cross-temporal cause-and-effect relationships (past causes with present consequences, and permanent/present traits with past consequences).

topics.title: High-Register Verb-Noun Collocations & Fixed Expressions (Locutions Verbales & Expressions Figées)
topics.objective: Synthesize, analyze, and deploy high-register multi-word verb-noun collocations and fixed idiomatic expressions (*prendre en compte*, *tenir compte de*, *faire état de*, *porter atteinte à*, *mettre en œuvre*, *rendre compte de*, *prendre du recul*) in formal, academic, legal, and professional contexts.
topics.spacy_pattern:
pattern = [
    # Pattern 1: prendre en compte
    [
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "prendre"},
        {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": "en"},
        {"LOWER": "compte"}
    ],
    # Pattern 2: tenir compte de / d' / du / des
    [
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "tenir"},
        {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": "compte"},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["de", "d'", "du", "des"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 3: faire état de / d' / du / des
    [
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "faire"},
        {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": "état"},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["de", "d'", "du", "des"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 4: porter atteinte à / au / aux / à l'
    [
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "porter"},
        {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": "atteinte"},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["à", "au", "aux", "a"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 5: mettre en œuvre / oeuvre
    [
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "mettre"},
        {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": "en"},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["œuvre", "oeuvre"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 6: (se) rendre compte de / d' / du / des
    [
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "rendre"},
        {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": "compte"},
        {"LOWER": {"IN": ["de", "d'", "du", "des"]}}
    ],
    # Pattern 7: prendre du recul
    [
        {"POS": {"IN": ["VERB", "AUX"]}, "LEMMA": "prendre"},
        {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
        {"LOWER": "du"},
        {"LOWER": "recul"}
    ]
]

topics.title: Rhetorical & Argumentative Patterns (Correlatives, Concessives & Infinitive Inversions)
topics.objective: Master high-level rhetorical and argumentative structures (*d'une part... d'autre part*, *non seulement... mais aussi/encore*, *tant... que*, *plus... plus*, *certes... mais*, *avoir beau + infinitif*) to construct nuanced, balanced, and persuasive formal prose.

topics.title: The Absolute Participle Clause (Le Participe Absolu / Proposition Participiale)
topics.objective: Form and master absolute participle clauses (*proposition participiale*) to express anterior or simultaneous temporal, causal, or conditional circumstances in formal prose with an independent noun subject and without linking conjunctions.
topics.spacy_pattern:
# spaCy Matcher pattern for Absolute Participle Clauses (Proposition Participiale)
pattern = [
    # Pattern 1: Optional adverbial trigger (Une fois / À peine) + Noun/Determiner + Past/Present Participle
    [
        {"LOWER": "une", "OP": "?"},
        {"LOWER": "fois", "OP": "?"},
        {"POS": "DET", "OP": "?"},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["NOUN", "PROPN"]}},
        {"POS": "ADV", "OP": "*"},
        {"POS": "VERB", "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["VerbForm=Part"]}},
        {"POS": "PUNCT", "LOWER": ","}
    ],
    # Pattern 2: Determiner + Noun + Aux (étant/ayant) + Past Participle
    [
        {"POS": "DET", "OP": "?"},
        {"POS": {"IN": ["NOUN", "PROPN"]}},
        {"POS": "AUX", "LEMMA": {"IN": ["être", "avoir"]}, "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["VerbForm=Part"]}},
        {"POS": "VERB", "MORPH": {"IS_SUPERSET": ["VerbForm=Part"]}},
        {"POS": "PUNCT", "LOWER": ","}
    ]
]

topics.title: Pronominal Verbs with Idiomatic Meaning Shifts (Les Verbes Pronominaux Idiomatiques)
topics.objective: Master high-register pronominal verbs whose meanings shift dramatically through fixed pronominal clitics (*se*) and adverbial pronouns (*en*, *y*), including *s'en aller*, *en vouloir à*, *s'en prendre à*, *se passer de*, *y tenir*, and *s'y connaître en*.

topics.title: Register & Stylistic Variation (Soutenu Syntax vs Informal Spoken Shortcuts)
topics.objective: Master the syntactic, morphological, and phonological contrasts between elevated formal French (*style soutenu*) and informal spoken shortcuts (*registre familier/familier parlé*), identifying formal introductory locutions and spoken elisions.
